Admission turns on a mailed smear card. You paint a strip with a pigment batch you own, post it to the registrar, and a grader reads it through a small spectrometer, keeping the reflectance curve. The curve is the seat; a strip already on file is refused, and renewal demands a fresh smear.

That reads like a banknote check: wrong ink weight shows even under a clean print. Here a ripple near 530 nm marks a knocked-off mix.

Per clone: 60 dollars for a distinct batch, 28 postage, 40 a reading, about 128 and a six to nine day voyage. Fifty clones costs 6,400 dollars before standing exists.
